newsitem.title: UK: Brazil features in new sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil features in new sugar freight orders.

text.p: Demand for Brazilian sugar featured again on the freight market on Thursday as the region gathered pace into its 1997 shipment cycle, shipbrokers said.

Cargill quoted for 14/20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Corinto to the Black Sea for the first half of June and Commodity Specialists for 24/25,000 tonnes from Puerto Quetzal to US Gulf/Atlantic for prompt dates.
E D & F Man was open for 13,000 tonnes in bags from south China to Pakistan for mid-June and a further 9/10,000 tonnes from Durban to east Africa for June 5/15.
Shipbrokers said Vitol was open for 25/28,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Morocco with options of Black Sea and Baltic.
Brazilian shippers SIMAB quoted for 25,000 tonnes from Recife to Black Sea/Egyptian Med for early June.
Of the day's firmer business, Tate & Lyle was said to have fixed 26,000 tonnes in bulk from Durban to Odessa for June 1/15 on the the Apj Anjli at a rate believed to be between $23 and $24.
Tate & Lyle was also said to have fixed 17,750/18,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Bridgetown to the U.K. but further details have yet to emerge.
